historical_references.context: Ibn Rushd, also known as Averroes, was a prominent philosopher, scholar and jurist of Islamic Spain. He is best known for his commentaries on Aristotle, which were influential in the Latin West. Ibn Rushd's works were translated into Latin during the 13th century and played a significant role in the development of Scholastic philosophy.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Battuta, Ibn Jubayr The name Ibn carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta and Ibn Jubayr were renowned travelers from the Islamic world. Ibn Battuta, born in Morocco, undertook a journey that covered over 75,000 miles, visiting numerous Islamic and non-Islamic lands. His Rihla, or travelogue, is a valuable historical source, providing detailed descriptions of various cultures and societies. Ibn Jubayr, born in Valencia, Spain, also embarked on an extensive journey, documenting his travels in The Travels of Ibn Jubayr. Both Ibn Battuta and Ibn Jubayr contributed significantly to the exploration and understanding of the world during the medieval period.
